data.text:
KIKO AT EDSA RALLY: 'TAUMBAYAN ANG PINAKAMAINAM NA SAFEGUARD SA PANG-AABUSO SA PUWESTO'

Sen. Kiko Pangilinan on Sunday, September 21, joined the protest at the EDSA People Power Monument against the multitrillion-peso flood control scandal, stressing that the mobilization of ordinary citizens is the strongest check on corruption.

"Walang puwersang mas hihigit pa sa usapin ng pulitika pag ang taumbayan na mismo ang naninindigan, tumataya, at kumikilos. 'Yan ang pinakamainam na safeguard sa pang-aabuso sa puwesto — ang taumbayan na kumikilos, naninindigan, at tumataya. Hindi papayag ang ating mga kababayan sa cover-up. Hindi papayag ang ating mga kababayan na walang mananagot," Pangilinan said.

The senator had earlier called on Filipinos to join "peaceful assemblies" to demand justice and accountability in light of mounting evidence of massive corruption in flood control projects. He emphasized that a united and mobilized citizenry is crucial in fighting abuse of power and uncovering the "whole truth" rather than a "sanitized version of the truth."

The "Trillion Peso March" brought tens of thousands to nationwide protest sites, including Luneta Park, the Rizal Shrine, and the EDSA Shrine, where Pangilinan first attended mass before joining the demonstration.

BUMOSES NA ANG MGA ARTISTA NG BAYAN! ✊

True to their words, “It’s Showtime” hosts Vice Ganda and Anne Curtis — both among the country’s top taxpayers — joined thousands of Filipinos in the streets on Sunday as they marched with the Angat Bayanihan Volunteer Network for the #TrillionPesoMarch in Quezon City.

The two were joined by Ion Perez, Jackie Gonzaga, Jasmine Curtis, Donny Pangilinan, and Darren Espanto, marching all the way to the People Power Monument on Sept. 21, the 53rd anniversary of martial law.

Earlier, at least 49,000 gathered at Rizal Park for the “Baha sa Luneta” rally, raging at ghost flood-control projects. Protesters later converged at EDSA as religious groups led a massive show of force at the historic site of the 1986 People Power Revolution.

UPDATE: 17 kataong responsable sa marahas na protesta sa Ayala Bridge, hawak na ng pulisya; kakasuhan — PNP | RH 52 @ednielparrosa, DZRH News

PNP STATEMENT

"The Philippine National Police has received reports of tension during today’s rally, including incidents of stone-throwing and a trailer truck being set on fire at Ayala corner Romualdez, Mendiola, where around 300–400 individuals had gathered. Seventeen individuals believed to be responsible are now in the custody of the Manila Police District. Firefighters and police personnel responded immediately, and the situation is now contained. Appropriate charges are being readied for filing against those involved.

We respect the public’s right to peaceful assembly, but we strongly appeal to everyone to remain calm and refrain from violence. Such actions endanger lives and undermine the message of those who wish to protest peacefully.

The PNP remains committed to safeguarding both the public and demonstrators. We will continue to exercise maximum tolerance, but we will also act against anyone who causes harm or damages property. Rest assured, those responsible for these acts will be held accountable under the law".

data.text:
Around 400 protesters gathered at Rizal Park in Tuguegarao City on Sunday, September 21, to denounce widespread corruption in government, including alleged anomalies in flood control projects.

The rally, held at 3 p.m., was led by the volunteer group Kabataan Kontra Korapsyon (KKK) with support from the Archdiocese of Tuguegarao and local advocates. Participants called for an end to graft and abuses in public service.

The demonstration coincided with a major anti-corruption campaign in Metro Manila. Protesters staged a brief parade from Rizal Park to nearby main roads and back.

Placards carried by the demonstrators bore messages such as: “Lead Fairly, Act Wisely, Inspire Many,” “Ikulong ang Korap (Jail the corrupt),” “Justice for All, Not Just a Few,” “Good Governance, Better Future,” and “Gutom lang ’yan (That's just hunger, Eat the Rich!” Passersby stopped to take photos of the striking slogans. | @VillVisayaJrINQ /PDI
